item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This thing really messes with your head. It makes you think about whether it's talking about 411's perspective or someone else's, and if you don't do that before trying to understand what you just read, everything just goes into utter confusion. "SCP-411 often can't recall what he will have for dinner that night." "That's because he hasn't had dinner yet! Wait…"

I honestly love SCPs that make me have to think to understand them. There's just something about confusion that just really fits with the SCP universe.

Edit: It also makes you wonder a few things. For example, if you want 411 to answer a specific question, what should you do? Do you have to keep it in your thoughts and simply hope he answers it? Would you have to approach him with the sole, unshakable intent of asking that question and hope he doesn't say anything to make you change your mind about asking it? Another example: he's 400 years old in his perspective, right? That's more than enough time for the Foundation to find out how to destroy 682. Does 411 remember how they finally manage it? They could ask him that, and to avoid a paradox, they could also ask when they manage it. More questions are popping up in my head as I type now. If 411 is alive now, and an XK-Class EOTW scenario occurs, would that kill 411 and cause a paradox, instantly becoming a ZK Reality Failure? Okay, I'm done now.

TL;DR: Too many questions…

item.content:encoded:
Nope. Here's how the convo goes MY perspective:

"Hi, I'm Legendary." -> His Answer -> My Question -> Repeat 2 & 3 -> "Goodbye"

Here's how it goes HIS perspective.

"eybdooG", which is a standard greeting. -> 3 & 2 taepeR, which is usual, and probably headache-inducing for him -> noitseuQ yM, which is the last one, but he doesn't know it yet. -> rewsnA siH, which, again, he has no idea is the last thing he'll get in. -> ".yradnegeL m'I ,iH", at which point he becomes emotionally distressed, but only then.

To expand:

I enter -> He is distressed -> "Hi, I'm Legendary." -> His distress goes away, like magic.

And that's assuming I only intro myself that one time. I might introduce myself EVERY time I see him, to make sure he remembers my name, or only at the end, so he'll remember it in the past. (EDIT: And I'd only do that by prompting, because I wouldn't know it would be the last meeting. I'D be distressed leaving). Enough people do that that it's very likely he won't EVER be certain of last meetings, simply because the mechanics behind any conversation are already FUBAR.

Although it does occur to me - how does he know that your first meeting is going to be your last if he has no memory of the past? Maybe he recognizes that introductions mean he's never going to see you again

.
Your future is his past. So after the first meeting (from your perspective) all other meetings must by definition occur in your future (his past) - ergo all other meetings must occur in his past.
In order for there to occur a meeting in his "unknown" future it would have to have occured in your perceived past - which is impossible if this is your first meeting.

At your last meeting all other meetings have occured in your past - his future. So he will not recognise you - it is for him your first meeting.
